topics.label: Introduction and lecture objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecturer, the course structure, and the key learning outcomes regarding cancer causation.

topics.label: Etiology of cancer: genetic, environmental, and epidemiological factors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how cancer arises through an interplay of endogenous mutations, inherited susceptibility, and environmental exposures documented by epidemiological variation.

topics.label: Biological and chemical mechanisms of carcinogenesis and tumor promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the specific molecular and cellular mechanisms by which infectious agents, chemical mutagens, radiation, and non-mutagenic promoters initiate and drive cancer development.

topics.label: Methodologies for identifying and testing carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro experimental approaches used to detect carcinogen exposure and evaluate carcinogenic potential.

topics.label: Conclusion and risk-benefit considerations
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture by summarizing key themes and discussing how carcinogenic risks are balanced against practical benefits in everyday life.
